subject.title: policy: repair required deny tool findings

question: Should Policy `doctor --fix` automatically add required deny-tool ids to root or agent `tools.deny` when `workspaceRepairs=true`, while skipping scoped inherited-root writes?
rationale: The implementation appears coherent, but the change intentionally alters tool availability from policy findings and therefore needs maintainer acceptance of the compatibility and security-boundary behavior.

options.title: Accept Guarded Mutation
options.body: Allow the new automatic repair because it is opt-in through `workspaceRepairs`, targets the reported root/agent deny path, and skips the scoped inherited-root case.

options.title: Keep Required Denies Detect-Only
options.body: Reject automatic mutation for this class and leave required-deny findings as review-required/manual until maintainers want policy to edit tool-deny config.

options.title: Narrow Further Before Merge
options.body: Require a smaller repair shape, such as agent-local-only writes or additional upgrade proof, before accepting root `tools.deny` mutation.

recommendation.title: Accept Guarded Mutation
recommendation.body: Allow the new automatic repair because it is opt-in through `workspaceRepairs`, targets the reported root/agent deny path, and skips the scoped inherited-root case.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main history points to vincentkoc for the existing Policy doctor repair baseline, while the remaining question is maintainer acceptance of the boundary.
